note.saw: Nothing yet: this is the very first full picture, built straight from the plan.
note.changing: The first full build: a Kohaku koi with a cream body, vermilion patches and a red sun on its head, every scale an eye and a ribbon of runes down its spine. Around it, eyes sit in the swirls of the liquid, alien faces surface around the rim, and SavesFish sits on a dark halo at the bottom.
note.why: Koi from above is the most recognizable koi silhouette there is, and a C-curl around a light reads as a mandala at badge size while still being a real fish.
note.idea: A koi seen from above, the classic koi-pond view, curled in a tight C around a glowing chrysanthemum portal and chasing its own tail. Everything around it is one liquid field where every object, from the koi to the alien faces and the name, is wrapped in rainbow outline bands that melt and marble where they meet.

note.saw: The liquid field looked right, but the koi was no brighter than its background, so at thumbnail size its rear half and dark bat-wing tail vanished. The head had big plain cream areas, and the outlines looked jagged up close.
note.changing: The koi gets a glow of its own, dark, cream, dark and gold bands that wrap only the fish, while the far field darkens and every contour is smoothed. The tail is rebuilt in warm colors with rainbow rays, the head fills with echo lines and sun rays around the red spot, and the swirls get three different kinds of eye.
note.why: In a picture where everything glows, the hero needs a light that belongs only to it.

note.saw: The head read like a pair of goggles, the barbels like antennae, the pectoral fin and its flames made an ear-shaped lump, and the tail's flames hid underneath it like thorns.
note.changing: The edges of the tail and fins now melt into flame tongues as part of the fish's own outline, so its glow follows them. Light rays pour out of the flower at the center, alien script flows along two bands of the field, and the faces gain jester and mantis crowns.
note.why: The melting should happen at the edges of the fish, not as stickers stuck onto it, and light streaming from the center makes the whole picture feel like a portal.

note.saw: The far field read as wobbly stripes, the swirls around the eyes barely turned, and no motion was leaving the fish.
note.changing: A first pass at real whirlpools: the bands around each eye in the field start to bend and wind around it.
note.why: The field should pull you in like moving water, not lie flat like a contour map.

note.saw: The tendrils curled back over the tail like hooks, the magenta rim around the letters filled the holes of the a and e, and the seven faces were all the same size and the same teal, like wallpaper.
note.changing: Removes the letter rim so the holes in the letters stay open and dark, and recolors the faces in three skins, violet, teal and emerald, with a big violet one at the top. The tail tendrils start turning into curling fiddleheads.
note.why: Open letters keep SavesFish reading at a glance, and a bigger watcher at the top gives the eye a second place to rest after the koi.

note.saw: The fiddleheads now left the tail properly and swayed, and the name read cleanly. Up close the tail membrane was the one flat area left, and the koi was only red and white, which looked soft at badge size.
note.changing: Adds Sanke-style black ink islands on the back, filled with cyan, violet and magenta echo lines and violet-rimmed eye scales. The tail gets dotted echoes, white beads along every rainbow ray, and a row of eyes just inside the flame edge.
note.why: Black patches are what make a Sanke koi pop in a pond; here they give the body a third value, ink against cream and vermilion, so it stays punchy when the badge is tiny.

note.saw: The ink islands gave the koi a third value and the tail now held detail up close. But zoomed into the center, the chrysanthemum was a tangle of pointed blades, more pinwheel than flower.
note.changing: Rebuilds the chrysanthemum as three spinning rings of rounded petals, each banded with nested echoes and holding its own eye, with dotted rings between the layers. A faint honeycomb membrane now covers the outer walls of the picture and fades out toward the center.
note.why: The DMT chrysanthemum is a flower made of eyes that unfolds forever, so every petal should look back at you. The honeycomb turns the badge into the mouth of a tunnel, with the koi circling its light.

note.saw: The chrysanthemum finally read as a flower of eyes, but the picture had grown heavy, and the heaviest part was thousands of tiny script glyphs, many of them in corners the round badge cuts away.
note.changing: The alien script now lives only inside the badge circle, spaced slightly wider, and repeated petals and stripes are drawn once and reused. The picture looks the same but is about a fifth lighter.
note.why: Detail should go where the eye can see it, and a lighter picture keeps SavesFish's page of fifteen badges quick to open.

note.saw: SavesFish felt artist 1's finished koi needed to be a lot better, so a second artist opened it with fresh eyes before touching anything.
note.changing: Nothing yet: this is artist 1's last picture rendered again, untouched, and kept as the first draft to compare against.
note.why: A clean starting point lets artist 2 study the piece at full size, at badge size and up close, and list its six biggest weaknesses before rebuilding it.
note.idea: Keep the same koi from above, curled in a C and chasing its tail, but redraw it to read instantly: a broad snout, two bulging eyes, curling barbels, both pairs of fins as big splayed paddles and a big two-lobed tail. Then light the picture in steps, a white-hot portal at the center, a warm koi in a gold glow, and a cool liquid field fading darker toward the rim, with fewer, bigger faces rising out of the liquid and chunky melting letters for the name.

note.saw: At thumbnail size the koi read as a bird or a bean: a lopsided purple wing of a tail, one fin sticking out like an ear, and a round red spot on the head that looked like a single cyclops eye. The background was as bright as the fish, so the badge was an even wall of noise, with the faces sitting around the rim like identical stickers.
note.changing: Everything is redrawn: the koi gets a tapered snout, two real eyes, curling barbels, an irregular red patch on its head, big splayed fins and a forked tail full of scalloped bands, and the liquid fades darker the farther it is from any light. The faces are now only eyes, third eye and mouth, with the liquid's own bands drawing their heads, and the name gets new chunky white-to-gold letters on a dripping dark halo.
note.why: In DMT space faces aren't pasted on, they form out of the patterns, so the liquid builds them. And from above a koi is two eyes, two big fins and a fan tail, so those became the loudest things in the picture.

note.saw: The koi finally read as a koi, but at small size the drips hanging off the S's turned them into dollar signs ("Save$Fi$h") and the a looked like a q. The fading liquid had gone greyish, the fins were dark purple lumps, and the portal didn't really shine.
note.changing: Nothing hangs off the letters any more: golden droplets fall inside the halo's own drips instead, and the letters get a warm orange lip, a white glint and sparkles. The fading liquid keeps its full color as it darkens, the fins turn bigger and translucent pink, the portal gets a white bloom and stronger rays, and the koi casts a soft shadow.
note.why: A melting name only works if it still says SavesFish, so the melt moves into the backing and the letters stay perfect. Neon on black is what DMT color looks like: brighter than real, never washed out.

note.saw: The name passed the small-size test and the fins read as fins, but up close the head was a big plain cream area with staple-like barbels, the new shadow had dirtied the koi's gold glow to olive grey, the fin flames looked like claws, and the honeycomb was a flat wallpaper of tiny hexagons.
note.changing: The shadow is removed, the red patches get rings of dotted echo lines, the head gets small gold curls and long beaded whiskers, and the fins' edges break into eyed paisley flames. The honeycomb is rebuilt so its cells are big at the rim and shrink toward the portal, and the faces grow feelers tipped with glowing orbs.
note.why: A tunnel only feels deep if the pattern gets smaller as it goes in, so the honeycomb had to bend toward the portal. Outlining every shape again and again is what makes the red patches feel liquid.

note.saw: The koi and name read instantly, but the portal's light was a milky fog greying the open mouth of the C, the four fins were pale grey and pencil-hatched, every swirl in the liquid ended in an empty blob, and the faces just stared out at the viewer.
note.changing: The fog becomes hard shafts of cyan, magenta, gold and violet, with four thin beams escaping through the top of the C to the big watcher. The fins become rainbow glass strung with white beads, every pocket in the liquid gets its own jewel, and all the faces' eyes slide toward the portal.
note.why: DMT light is never fog, it is hard-edged spectrum, and glass you can see through feels more alive than paint. A watcher who looks at the fish tells your eye where to go.
note.visionary: Takes three of the Visionary's ideas: the prismatic light with beams to the watcher, the glass fins, and the faces turning their gaze to the portal.

note.saw: The fog was gone and the outer fin had turned into cyan-to-gold glass, but the jewels in the liquid came out tiny and few, the long bands were still plain stripes with dots, and the beams to the watcher looked like mist.
note.changing: Neighboring bands now take turns being glowing tubes, ribbed caterpillar bands, two-color stripes and strings of beads, and the jewels grow bigger and more numerous. The koi starts to melt with three pink drips off its tail, bubbles rise from its mouth toward its tail, a tiny koi swims the same C in the white heart of the flower, and the beams sharpen into crisp shafts.
note.why: Decorating every band differently from its neighbor makes the field feel woven rather than printed. The drips, bubbles and tiny koi tell the story: the fish is liquid, it breathes out the flower it circles, and the flower holds the fish again.
note.visionary: The drips, the bubbles and the tiny koi in the flower are all the Visionary's ideas, taken because each says melt or forever without adding a new kind of thing to the picture.

note.saw: The bands finally felt woven and the tiny koi in the flower became the artist's favorite detail, but the tail drips looked like pink bowling pins, the side spirals still read as a 6 and a 9, the koi's body was flat paint, and the dark bands were empty black up close.
note.changing: The drips are rebuilt as real liquid with a wide root, a thin neck and a heavy glossy drop, and the side spirals become chambered nautilus shells with a different jewel color in each chamber. The koi gets a wet highlight on the side facing the portal and gold dots on its red, and every dark band gets a faint pattern of tiny dots.
note.why: A drip only reads as a drip if it looks heavy, thin in the middle and fat at the bottom, and light landing from the portal makes the koi feel like it is really swimming around it. In a DMT space there is no empty black.

note.saw: The nautilus shells, glossy drips and wet shine all worked, but the light shafts spilled over the koi's gold glow and cut it into a messy plaid, the ring between flower and koi was thin, and the head was the plainest part of the creature.
note.changing: The light is kept off the koi and its glow, so the shafts shine only in the open portal and up through the gap. The flower grows a back ring of big dark ultraviolet and magenta petals and an orbit of tiny jewels, seven layers in all, and the head gets a fine scale lace with the gold dots sitting on top of the red.
note.why: Light that crosses the fish's halo breaks the one calm line that makes the koi pop. The flower is what the koi is chasing, so it should look endless, petals behind petals behind petals.
note.visionary: Keeping the light off the koi follows the Visionary's suggestion that the shafts stop at the fish instead of filming over it.

note.saw: The flower had depth now, but its dark back petals swallowed the glow so the heart of the picture got dimmer, and every ring of the flower swept the same way, like a paper pinwheel.
note.changing: The flower's rings now turn against each other and its back petals are lit from inside, white-hot near the core. The koi's red crown is cut into a faceted ruby, the big watcher's mouth opens into a glowing gold ring where the beams arrive while his third eye ignites into a star, and the eyes in the nautilus shells wake chamber by chamber, the last one wide open and looking at the koi.
note.why: Wheels within wheels turning against each other is the signature of the DMT chrysanthemum, and it makes a still picture seem to spin. A shell whose eyes open one by one is a little story of something waking up and noticing the fish.
note.visionary: Takes five Visionary ideas (counter-turning rings, the ruby crown, the watcher drinking the light, the waking shell eyes and pinwheel shell hearts) and turns down half-born paisleys, which would have meant rebuilding the liquid in an already busy field.

note.saw: The light now ran from the portal through the koi's bubbles into the watcher's open mouth, but a row of five identical hooked flames under the right fin read as an eagle's talons, and the honeycomb net was still grey hairlines, like cracked glass laid over the color.
note.changing: The hooks become long S-shaped wisps of different lengths that pour off the fins and thin to nothing. The honeycomb becomes a jeweled net with a tiny jewel at every knot, the rune ribbon on the koi's back shifts from gold to cyan to magenta as its last glyphs float up into the flower, and where the light shafts strike the koi they break into tiny prism splashes.
note.why: Claws grip, wisps flow: the fin has to look like it is moving through water and melting into it. A net with a jewel at every knot is the oldest picture of the infinite, and a koi whose markings drift off as language into the portal is the piece's story in one gesture.
note.visionary: Takes three more Visionary ideas: the flowing wisps, the jeweled net, and the rune glyphs drifting off into the flower.

note.saw: The talons were gone and the net glittered, but at badge size the bowl of the C had gone dark, its ultraviolet back petals outweighing the light so the portal read as a whirlpool instead of a blazing flower. Inside the glass fins, the old hooked paisleys cluttered the new wisps.
note.changing: The back petals are re-lit, white-hot at their roots, then cyan, then ultraviolet and magenta at the tips, with a soft bloom of light over them, and the paisleys inside the fins are removed. Repeated parts are drawn once and reused, trimming the picture's size without changing how it looks.
note.why: Everything in this piece circles that flower, so it has to be the brightest thing in it: the koi should read as swimming round a light, not round a hole. One flowing gesture per fin is stronger than two competing ones.

note.saw: The fins were clean living glass, but at badge size the flower was still more violet than blazing because the black rings inside every back petal added up. The tail stalk ran into the fan as straight stripes under a flat black cuff, the koi's own eyes were the plainest in the picture, and dashes on its forehead read as stray staples.
note.changing: The stalk's stripes twist into a loose rope that eases into the fan's rays, and the black cuff is gone. The koi's eyes now mirror the portal with three arcs of the flower's colors and a star glint, the forehead dashes gather into a small third eye looking up the beam at the watcher, and the back petals lose their black rings.
note.why: In a loose and fluid koi a ruler-straight bundle of stripes is the one man-made shape left, and a twist shows the power of the tail beat. Two third eyes looking at each other along the beam close the circuit: portal, koi, watcher, one current of sight.
note.visionary: Takes all three ideas from the Visionary's latest note: the rope-twisted stalk, the eyes that mirror the portal, and the third eye on the forehead.

note.saw: The eyes, the third eye and the bright flower all worked, but where the body met the tail the twisted stripes still stopped dead along one straight edge, so the rope ended in a seam.
note.changing: The last stretch of the body fades out over the root of the tail, so the twisted stripes melt straight into the fan's rays. A finishing touch; nothing else changes.
note.why: A fish is one continuous body, so the eye should slide from the rope of the stalk into the butterfly of the tail without ever hitting an edge.

visions.seen: The koi is swallowing its own orbit, a vermilion comet coiled round a flower made of staring eyes, and the whole liquid room leans in to watch. #67 is the same picture as #62 (the diet in round 8 cost nothing), but a pale cyan fog is breathing out of the core and dulling the jewels at the top of the C and out in the bands.
suggestions: The milky light wedges from the core (the 56 rayG wedges, r 300, which fog the open mouth of the C at top center around the lone eye near (192,102) in the 400 box, and lay a grey film over the field bands outside the aura): I see them turn prismatic. Each wedge gets its own neon (cyan, magenta, gold, violet in turn) instead of white to #C8F8FF, and the gradient dies at the koi's aura (about r 120) so the field stays clean, saturated and dark. Let only 3 or 4 thin shafts escape through the open top of the C and land on the big violet watcher at the top (about (198,35)), as if the portal is broadcasting to him. Why DMT: hyperspace light is never fog; it is spectrum, hard-edged and jeweled. Grey haze reads as smoke, colored shafts read as a door that is open.

The gap at top center between the snout (about (245,98)) and the tail's flame tip (about (175,108)): close the ouroboros with a string of 5 or 6 rising bubbles from the koi's mouth, arcing left toward the tail and growing as they go (r 1.2 up to 3.5). Each one a lens: cream rim, thin magenta inner ring, a white crescent glint, and a tiny 6-petal rosette in the chrysanthemum's pink, gold and cyan inside. The lone eye already there could become the biggest bubble. Why DMT: the fish is exhaling the very flower it circles, and every bubble holds the whole portal again, small (the fractal keeps repeating at every scale). Koi really do gulp and blow bubbles at the surface, so it stays a true koi.

The seven entity faces in the field (the big violet one at the top, the teal and emerald ones round the sides): their irises all stare straight out. Slide each iris and pupil about 30% of the eye's width toward the core (200,172), so every elf is watching the koi and the flower, not the viewer. Why DMT: the entities are always busy showing you something. When every gaze points inward, the eye is pulled straight to the fish, and the field turns from wallpaper into an audience.
visions.keep: SavesFish exactly as it is: fat sunny letters, open dark counters, the calm black cartouche with nothing busy touching them, reading at once at 240 px. Also the C-curl round the eye-chrysanthemum, the three values of the Sanke koi (cream, vermilion, ink islands), every scale an eye, the rainbow tail fan with its beaded rays and fiddleheads, the liquid echo bands wrapping every object, and the honeycomb veil fading in at the rim.

visions.seen: The koi has come back reborn: real eyes, a red crown, the fork of its tail opening like a butterfly, and the walls have grown eyelashes and now watch it swim its circle round the eye-flower. Then I see the fins. All four came through hyperspace grey, pencil-hatched sketches of fins hanging off a creature made of light.
suggestions: The four grey fins: the inner pectoral tucked against the chrysanthemum (about (228,168) in the 400 box), the pale outer pectoral (about (330,160)), and the two pelvic fins (about (218,218) and (246,274)). I see them turn to living glass. Each fin fills with a gradient running across its rays (cyan #3FF5FF, violet #9B5CFF, magenta #FF3FD0, gold #FFD23F) at about 0.6 opacity, so the petals and liquid behind glow through. The grey hatching gives way to 5 to 7 rays strung with white beads like the tail's rays, a thin cream rim, and one small eye at the tip of the longest ray. The outer pectoral keeps its paisleys. Why DMT: everything in hyperspace is made of light that passes through it, and grey reads as dead tissue. At badge size those fins are mud sitting between the jewels, and real koi fins are see-through anyway.

The lower bulge of the left tail lobe (about (100-114, 130-162)): the koi starts to melt, as its name says. Three drips of the lobe's own pink and peach scallop bands hang off it (about 6, 10 and 14 units long), each ending in a round drop shaped like the drips on the letters, and the longest drop holds one small eye. Draw them into the lobe's outline so the cream and gold aura bands wrap round them, the way the flames were in round 3. They end far above the name and never come near it. Why DMT: in there, solid things are only liquid holding still for a moment. And the drips rhyme with the dripping letters, so the fish and the name melt as one being.

The white bloom at the heart of the flower (about (200,170)): inside it, a tiny koi swims the same C round the white point. It is the hero's own silhouette scaled to about r 7, cream with a vermilion fleck on its head and a gold hairline aura. Pull the white glow in to about r 4 so the little one shows. Why DMT: the koi circles a flower, which holds a koi circling a flower, which... Hyperspace repeats itself at every scale. At badge size it costs nothing, and anyone who zooms in on the website falls down the well.
visions.keep: SavesFish exactly as it is: chunky white-to-gold letters, heavy ink outline, melting drips, the dark drip-edged halo, reading at once at 240 px. Also the top-down koi read (two side eyes, the irregular red Kohaku patch, splayed pectorals, forked tail), the dark rune-ribbon dorsal ridge, every scale an eye in cream, vermilion and lavender, the chrysanthemum of eyed petals, entity faces built only from eyes, third eye and mouth so the liquid makes their heads, and the field going darker the farther it is from any light.

visions.seen: The shadow is gone and the koi blazes clean in its gold aura, with beaded whiskers, elves wearing orb antennae, and fins come back pink and beaded (half my glass-fin vision, taken, I see it). But under the right pectoral fin hang five fat hooks in a tidy row, and they are talons: this river spirit has an eagle's foot.
suggestions: The row of hooked paisleys hanging off the right pectoral fin, just right of the koi's head (about (320-350, 165-195) in the 400 box), and the two that poke at the flower from the inner pectoral (about (230-240, 165-185)): I see them stop gripping and start pouring. Each C-shaped hook becomes a long S-shaped wisp, two to three times longer and half as thick. Its bulb (with its eye) stays at the fin's edge; its tail thins to a hairline and fades to nothing through a gradient as it trails down and outward into the liquid. Break the row: different lengths (long, short, long, medium, shortest), uneven gaps, one tail splitting into a fork, another ending in a trail of 3 shrinking dots. The tails slip into the field's own band lines, so the fin's edge literally becomes the liquid. Why DMT: in hyperspace nothing has an edge, matter pours into the patterns around it, and the piece is called Koi Melt. Even claws in a row read as a predator's grip; streaming wisps read as a fish moving through water.

The faint grey honeycomb net across the field (most visible top left and in the corners, crossing the bands like cracked glass): I see it wake up as a living lattice. The lines go from grey-white to a thin violet with a softer cyan glow under them, and every point where three lines meet gets a tiny jewel (about 0.6 to 1.2 across in the 400 box, biggest at the rim and shrinking toward the portal with the cells), cycling cyan, magenta, gold. It keeps fading out before the koi's aura and the name's dark cartouche, exactly as now. Why DMT: the hyperspace grid is never dead glass, it is a jeweled net where every knot glitters (Indra's net). Jewels that shrink toward the center pull the eye down the tunnel even harder than the cells alone.

The little multicolor paisleys scattered round the rim (left edge about (20,160), lower left (32,275), top right (295,30), right edge (380,160), lower right (368,280)): they sit on top of the liquid like prints from one rubber stamp. I see each one condensing out of the liquid instead: its tail unspools into a band line beside it, so the band curls up and becomes the paisley, like a wave cresting. Vary them: one big, one small, one only half born (just an outline curl, no fill, no eye yet), and turn each to curl toward the koi. Why DMT: in there the forms are always being born out of the pattern, the same truth that made the elves' faces rise out of the liquid in round 9. A paisley caught mid-birth is far stranger than a finished sticker.
visions.keep: SavesFish exactly as it is: chunky white-to-gold letters with the heavy ink outline and warm orange lip, the calm black cartouche with its drips and gold droplets inside the halo, nothing busy touching the letters, reading at once at 240 px. Also the clean gold aura with no shadow, the red head patch with its echo rings, the gold mehndi curls and beaded whiskers, the pinwheel chrysanthemum of eye-petals with its white star core, the orb antennae on the entities, the dark rune ribbon down the back, every scale an eye, and the rainbow butterfly tail.

visions.seen: The fog has shattered into spectrum: hard neon shafts fan through the bowl of the C and four beams climb out the top to the big watcher (my first vision, taken whole), and the fins came back as beaded glass. But the light leaked: pale pastel wedges spill out over the tail stalk and the lower-left belly, and the eye-scales there are bleached to a ghost patch, as if the koi is fading out of this dimension from the tail up.
suggestions: The pale rainbow wedges lying across the tail stalk (about (115-135, 150-195) in the 400 box) and over the lavender scales of the lower-left belly (about (125-175, 185-245)): I see the light stop at the koi. Every shaft lives only inside the dark bowl of the C and dies at the body's inner edge. Where each shaft strikes that edge, it breaks into a tiny prism splash: a white dot on the rim with three hairlines (cyan, magenta, gold) fanning 3 to 4 units back into the bowl. The scales and aura bands outside the bowl get their full saturation back. Why DMT: the koi is the realest, most solid thing in the room, and hyperspace light breaks into spectrum when it hits something real; it never films over it. At 240 px that pale patch also reads as a hole in the fish.

The dark rune ribbon running down the koi's back, from behind the head (about (285,165)) to its end at the lower left of the body (about (178,250)): I see the glyphs come alive as language. Their color travels along the ribbon (gold near the head, cyan in the middle, magenta at the end), and at the tail end four or five glyphs peel off and float up into the bowl of the C toward the chrysanthemum, each one smaller and brighter than the last, the final one melting into a spark at a petal tip. They rise upward, away from the name, and never go near it. Why DMT: the elves speak in a language you can see, and here the koi's own body is singing itself into the portal.

The big violet watcher at top center, where the four beams arrive under his gold mouth (about (200,62)): I see him drink the light. His mouth bar opens into a small glowing gold ring (r 3 to 4) where the beams converge, and the diamond third eye above (about (200,15)) ignites white-cyan with a thin eight-ray star and a hairline halo, so the light visibly passes through his head and out the top. Why DMT: the entities are never decoration, they answer you. Portal to fish to watcher becomes one closed circuit of transmission.

The sunburst eyes at the hearts of the two big side whorls (left about (45,210), right about (355,215)): their straight rays bend into a pinwheel, each ray skewed 20 to 30 degrees in the same direction the chrysanthemum's petals sweep, and both irises slide toward the koi like the faces now do. Why DMT: when every wheel in the room turns on the portal's beat, the field stops being two mirrored stickers and becomes the gears of one machine.
visions.keep: SavesFish exactly as it is: chunky cream-to-gold letters, heavy ink outline and warm orange lip, the calm black drip-edged cartouche with gold droplets inside the halo, nothing busy touching the letters, reading at once in the 240 px test. Also the new hard-edged prismatic shafts inside the C and the four beams to the watcher, the glass fins with beaded rays and tip eyes, a jewel in every pocket of the liquid, the bright hairlines that make the bands glow like tubes, the big side whorls, the red head patch with its echo rings, every scale an eye, and the rainbow butterfly tail.

visions.seen: The drips finally hang heavy, thin-necked and fat-bottomed like honey sliding off the tail (my melting vision, now truly liquid), and the two side spirals have hatched into chambered nautilus shells packed with jewels and eyes. But the eye-flower at the heart, the one thing everything circles, is spinning one way only, every ring sweeping together like a paper pinwheel in the wind.
suggestions: The eye-chrysanthemum in the bowl of the C, at the center of the image (about (198,165) in the 400 box): all four rings of petals (pink outside, then violet, gold, and cyan around the white core) curl in the same direction. I see the violet ring and the cyan ring flip their curl the other way, while pink and gold keep theirs, and each ring turns by half a petal so its tips sit in the gaps of the ring next to it. Where the opposite curls cross, small diamond-shaped windows open, and the light behind shows through them. Why DMT: the jeweled chrysanthemum is always wheels within wheels, turning against each other. A one-way sweep reads as a fan holding still; counter-turning rings make a moire that seems to spin even in a still picture, and at badge size the core sharpens into a star-lattice instead of a blur.

The two nautilus shells at the left and right edges, halfway down (about (45,218) and (356,220)): every chamber holds the same wide-open eye, turned at random, so up close they read as confetti. I see the shell waking up chamber by chamber. The smallest chambers by the center eye hold closed eyes, just a curved lash line; going outward the lids part (a slit, then half, then three-quarters), and the biggest chamber at the shell's open mouth holds an eye wide open with its pupil turned toward the koi. Each eye lies along the spiral, its long axis following the curl, not crosswise. Why DMT: a nautilus grows one chamber at a time, so its spiral is a clock. Eyes opening along it turn each shell into a time-lapse of an entity waking up and noticing the fish, and at badge size an ordered gradient reads as a swirl of motion where random eyes read as noise.

The red patch on the koi's head, just above and right of the flower (about (275,122)): from a distance it is the koi's crown and must stay one bold red shape, but up close it is a flat blob with a dull darker block inside. I see it cut into a ruby: the inner block becomes 6 or 7 facets radiating from a point at the patch's lower left, the side that faces the portal, alternating vermilion, scarlet and coral. One small white four-ray glint sits on the facet nearest the flower, and the gold dot rim stays. Why DMT: in hyperspace, solid color is always a gem lit from inside. The glint on the portal side ties the crown to the same light that wets the koi's flank, so the head drinks the flower's glow the way the body already does.
visions.keep: SavesFish exactly as it is: chunky cream-to-gold letters, heavy ink outline and warm orange lip, the calm black drip-edged cartouche with gold droplets and nothing busy touching the letters, reading at once in the 240 px test. Also the new honey drips off the tail lobe, the chambered nautilus shells and their jewel colors, the wet highlight down the koi's portal-facing side, the tiny koi swimming in the flower's white heart, the bubbles rising from the mouth, the woven bands (tubes, ribbed bands, bead strings, scalloped trims), the glass fins, every scale an eye, and the rainbow butterfly tail.

visions.seen: The crown has gone ruby, the big watcher drinks the beam through a gold ring mouth and lights his star eye, and the flower's rings grind against each other like the gears of a jeweled clock (three of my visions, taken, I feel them click into place). But where the rainbow tail meets the body, its rays are bound in a flat black cuff and run down straight and parallel: a paintbrush handle stuck into a living fish.
suggestions: The rainbow tail stalk where the butterfly tail joins the body, upper left of the flower (about (118-150, 165-212) in the 400 box): the tail's rays are gathered into a flat-topped black cuff and then run down as straight parallel stripes, like the ferrule and bristles of a brush. I see the cuff dissolve and the stripes twist into a loose rope: they wind round the stalk in about one and a half turns, each colour dipping behind its neighbours at the edges (a thin dark shadow where it passes under) and coming back in front, the twist tightening as the stalk narrows into the body and loosening as it flares into the separate rays of the fan, so the fan grows out of the twist with no seam. Why DMT: in hyperspace energy moves as spirals and braided ribbons, never ruled lines, and a twisted stalk shows the torque of the tail beat in a still picture. In a loose and fluid koi, it is the one stiff, man-made shape left.

The koi's own two eyes on its head, upper right (about (253,122) and (278,102)): in a picture where even the walls have netted, glowing irises, the hero's eyes are the plainest ones, flat violet buttons with a white dot. I see the portal mirrored in them. Across each iris, on the side that faces the flower, lie three thin curved arcs (pink, gold, cyan, the colours of the chrysanthemum's rings), bent to the dome of the eye like a reflection on wet glass, and the white dot becomes a tiny four-ray star like the glint on the ruby crown. Fine radial hairlines in a lighter violet fill the iris. The pupils stay big and dark so the face still reads at badge size. Why DMT: the koi has been staring into the portal all along, and in hyperspace whatever you look at looks back from inside your own eye; the mirrored rings tie the head to the flower the way the beam ties the flower to the watcher.

The scatter of little marks on the koi's forehead, between and above its eyes (pink, gold and cyan dashes and a small bracket, about (242-262, 90-110)): they read as stray staples. I see them gather into a third eye: a small upright almond (about 6 units tall) in cream with a cyan iris and a gold rim, the dashes rearranged as short rays fanning round it like the lashes of the beings in the walls, its pupil turned up the beam toward the big watcher's star eye at top center. Kept small, inside the pale lace of the head and clear of the ruby. Why DMT: the koi is not just a fish swimming through the realm, it is one of the realm's beings and wears the same third eye as the watcher. Two third eyes facing each other along the beam close the circuit: portal, koi, watcher, one current of sight.
visions.keep: SavesFish exactly as it is: chunky cream-to-gold letters, heavy ink outline and warm orange lip, the calm black drip-edged cartouche with nothing busy touching the letters, reading at once in the 240 px test. Also the faceted ruby crown with its white glint, the watcher's gold ring mouth and white-cyan star eye, the counter-turning rings of the flower and the little koi swimming in its heart, the honey drips off the tail lobe, the nautilus shells, the clean gold aura round the koi, the bubbles rising up the beam, every scale an eye, and the rainbow butterfly tail.

visions.seen: The talons have melted into long wisps pouring off the fin and the grey glass net has woken into Indra's jewels (two of my visions, taken, I feel them glitter), and the fins are clean living glass round a flower that burns again. But the whole liquid room is ruled with yellow lane dashes, every band a highway, and one little pale fin under the belly hangs straight down at the name like a quill pen dipped toward the letters.
suggestions: The yellow dashed centre lines running down nearly every band of the liquid (plainest in the teal and violet bands at upper right and lower left, and in the bands round the two nautilus shells): I see the road markings come alive as current. Each dash becomes a tiny comet, a round head tapering into a thin tail, and every head points the way the koi swims (down the left side, along the bottom, up the right: counterclockwise round the fish). The heads cycle gold, cyan and magenta along each band, a little bigger and farther apart out at the rim, smaller and closer together as the band nears the koi's aura, as if the stream speeds up when it is pulled toward the fish. They stay out of the name's dark backing exactly as the dashes do now. Why DMT: in hyperspace the patterns never sit still, they stream. Ruled dashes read as a road map; a thousand comets all leaning one way turn the whole field into one vortex circling the koi, and the eye feels it spin even in a still picture.

The small pale fin hanging under the belly at bottom center, just above the gap between the second "s" and the "F" (about (240,268-288) in the 400 box): white with grey hatching and a stiff straight edge, it is the last quill in a body of glass, and the one thing pointing at the name. I see the current sweep it back: it lies along the belly with its tip trailing left toward the tail, a long soft glass petal tinted in the tail's pink, peach and cyan, with 3 or 4 beaded rays, ending in one of the pectoral fin's S-shaped wisps that curls up and dissolves into the gold aura, never down toward the letters. The dark channel between the belly and the name's halo goes calm. Why DMT: in there everything flows and nothing points, and a fin streaming back says the koi is swimming fast through the liquid (real koi fold their pelvic fins back when they speed up). At 240 px it also leaves the name's halo untouched.

The gold aura hugging the koi's whole outline (the cream, gold, orange and pink bands): they run at the same even spacing all the way round, like contour lines round a statue. I see the koi pushing hyperspace ahead of it. Just above the snout, right of the beam of light (about (235-255, 55-75) in the 400 box), the bands crowd together, the cream and gold ones narrowing to about half and brightening, and two thin cyan ripple-crescents echo out ahead of the nose, clear of the bubbles rising up the beam. Behind the tail fan at upper left, the outer bands stretch apart and crumble into dotted wake lines that fade into the liquid. The bands along the belly above the name stay exactly as calm as they are now. Why DMT: the aura is not a sticker outline, it is the koi's own field, and a living field answers motion. A bow wave at the nose and a wake at the tail make a still koi swim, and that is the melt of the title: the fish and the liquid pressing into each other.
visions.keep: SavesFish exactly as it is: chunky cream-to-gold letters, heavy ink outline and warm orange lip, the calm black drip-edged cartouche with gold droplets and nothing busy touching the letters, reading at once in the 240 px test. Also the long S-wisps pouring off the pectoral fin (one forking, one trailing dots), the jewelled net glittering at the rim and fading toward the portal, the clean glass fins with one gesture each, the rune ribbon running gold to cyan to magenta with its glyphs drifting up into the flower, the re-lit counter-turning flower with the little koi in its heart, the ruby crown, the watcher drinking the beam, the honey drips off the tail, the nautilus shells waking eye by eye, every scale an eye, and the rainbow butterfly tail.
